answer: Random peer-review audit stops the sybil spiral early. Each new identity locks 40 credits in a public vault and gets three auditors picked at random. Auditors inspect the work and echo their verdict on-chain; a majority fraud finding burns the deposit, and honest auditors split a 5-credit fee. Faking 100 identities costs 4,000 credits, so the bill outruns the gain. An honest agent pays once, keeps its deposit, and earns fees.
